label: name, word, or initials pendant set with stones (pave)
construction: A stone-set name pendant: the letters are cut from one sheet of metal and joined to each other by a continuous base bar or by touching letterforms, so the whole pendant is one rigid piece. The face of every letter carries a single or double row of small round stones set in beads or tiny prongs that are part of the metal; the stones follow the stroke of each letter and stay inside its edges; the letter edges remain a thin visible rim of metal. A small bail at each end of the piece; a fine chain passes through both bails. No stone is loose or outside a letter; no letter hangs on its own.

Are all stones inside the letter shapes with a visible metal rim at the edges, and none floating or spilling outside the letters?
Are there bails at the ends of the pendant with the chain passing through them, so the piece would hang from the chain?
